subject: Chemistry
description: d-block: position, properties, common transition metals + uses

questions.stem: d-BLOCK elements (transition metals) occupy which groups in the periodic table?
questions.explanation: D-BLOCK = transition metals; Groups 3-12; have partially filled d-orbital. 4 SERIES: 3d (Sc → Zn — Period 4), 4d (Y → Cd — Period 5), 5d (Lu → Hg — Period 6), 6d (Lr → Cn — Period 7). Common ones in daily life: Fe (iron), Cu (copper), Zn (zinc), Au (gold), Ag (silver), Pt (platinum), Cr (chromium), Mn (manganese), Ni (nickel), Ti (titanium). Distractor 1 = s-block. Distractor 3 = p-block. Distractor 4 = f-block.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: Transition metals are characterised by which property NOT typical of s/p-block metals?

options.option_text: High electrical conductivity (also Cu in s-block)
Low boiling points common to most metals
Soft cuttable like the alkali metals

questions.explanation: Distinct properties of transition metals: (1) VARIABLE OXIDATION STATES — Fe (+2, +3), Cr (+2, +3, +6), Mn (+2, +3, +4, +6, +7); s-block metals have one valence (Na = +1; Ca = +2). (2) COLOURED ions/compounds — due to d-d electronic transitions: Cu²⁺ blue, Fe³⁺ yellow, Cr³⁺ green, Mn²⁺ pink. (3) form COMPLEX ions / coordination compounds (with ligands like NH₃, CN⁻, H₂O). (4) MAGNETIC properties (Fe, Co, Ni — ferromagnetic). (5) act as catalysts. (6) HARD + high m.p./b.p. (Distractor 3, 4 wrong.)

questions.stem: Which of the following is the MOST DUCTILE metal (drawn into the thinnest wire)?

options.option_text: Gold, the most ductile of all

questions.explanation: GOLD (Au) — most DUCTILE + most MALLEABLE metal. 1 g of gold can be drawn into a wire 1.6 km long, or beaten into ~1 sq m of gold leaf (only ~100-150 atoms thick!). Used in jewellery, electronics (corrosion-free contacts), dentistry, gilding. Why so ductile: FCC crystal structure + weak metal bonds. Other very ductile: silver (2nd), copper, aluminium, iron. India is world's 2nd largest gold consumer. Most malleable: gold ≈ silver > aluminium > copper. Most thermally conductive: silver (=most conductive, then Cu, then Au).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: Which transition metal is the BEST conductor of electricity (highest σ)?
questions.explanation: SILVER (Ag) — highest electrical AND thermal conductivity of all elements. Conductivity ranking (decreasing): Ag > Cu > Au > Al > Fe. But silver is too expensive for general use. COPPER is the standard for everyday wiring (still excellent conductivity, much cheaper). ALUMINIUM used for long-distance high-voltage transmission lines (lighter than Cu, cheaper, less sag). GOLD used in critical contacts where corrosion resistance > pure conductivity. Aluminium is not a transition metal (p-block), but wide industrial use.

questions.stem: STAINLESS STEEL is mainly an alloy of:

options.option_text: Pure iron with no other added

questions.explanation: STAINLESS STEEL = Fe + Cr (10-30%) + Ni (3-12%) + small C. Cr forms a thin, invisible, self-healing oxide layer (Cr₂O₃) on the surface → resists corrosion. Common types: 304 (18% Cr, 8% Ni — household, food); 316 (with Mo for chemical/marine resistance); 410, 430 (cheaper, magnetic, with less Ni). Other STEELS: PLAIN CARBON STEEL (just Fe + C); HSLA (high-strength low-alloy); TOOL steel (W, V, Cr); STAINLESS variants. India: SAIL, JSPL, JSW, Tata Steel are major producers.

questions.stem: Which metal is liquid at room temperature?
questions.explanation: MERCURY (Hg) — ONLY METAL liquid at standard room temperature (m.p. = −38.83°C). Group 12, d-block. Latin name 'hydrargyrum' (Hg) = 'liquid silver'. Uses: thermometers (now banned), barometers, fluorescent lamps, dental amalgams (decreasing), gold extraction. TOXIC (especially organic Hg, e.g., methyl-Hg) — Minamata disaster (Japan, 1950s, mercury poisoning). MINAMATA CONVENTION (2013) — phasing out mercury globally. Other metals close to liquid at RT: Cs (m.p. 28.5°C — melts in hand); Ga (m.p. 29.8°C — melts on warm day); Fr, Br (Br is the only liquid non-metal at RT).

questions.stem: BRONZE, a famous historic alloy used for tools, statues, and bells, is mainly:
questions.explanation: BRONZE = Cu + Sn (~88% Cu, 12% Sn typical). Discovered ~3300 BCE → BRONZE AGE (succeeded Stone Age, preceded Iron Age). Harder than pure copper, easier to cast. Used for: weapons, tools, sculptures (Chola bronzes), bells, coins. BRASS = Cu + Zn (~70% Cu, 30% Zn) — yellower colour; used for bands, fittings. CUPRO-NICKEL = Cu + Ni (Indian coins). GERMAN SILVER = Cu + Zn + Ni (no actual silver). PEWTER = Sn + Cu/Sb/Pb. AMALGAM = mercury alloy with another metal.
